summary.headline: Bajaj Electricals Q4 FY26 was modest: Lighting Solutions EBIT margin 8.7% in Q4 and record 8.5% for the year, while Consumer Products posted a loss on deleverage.
summary.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 as a modest quarter, hit by a delayed summer, geopolitical uncertainty, supply chain disruption and input cost inflation. Lighting Solutions grew 16% in Q4 with an 8.7% EBIT margin, and annual turnover rose 9.5% with EBIT up 28% and a record 8.5% annual margin. Consumer Products bore the brunt: fans and coolers declined, kitchen appliances grew about 30%, and the vertical reported a loss from operating deleverage. The company entered wires in February 2026, ended FY26 with INR 934 crore of cash, and kept negative working capital, with about INR 400 crore of operating cash flow in the quarter. A final dividend of INR 3 per share (150% of face value) was recommended.

financial_highlights.metric: Lighting Solutions FY26 annual EBIT margin

financial_highlights.value: INR 3 per share (150% of INR 2 face value)

segments.name: Lighting Solutions
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue up 16% with 8.7% EBIT margin; FY26 turnover up 9.5% and EBIT up 28% to a record 8.5% margin. Driven by premium mix; wires category launched in February 2026 with early orders and traction, sub-segments including Professional and Consumer Lighting both grew.

segments.name: Consumer Products
segments.commentary: Q4 was weak and reported a loss on operating deleverage. Kitchen appliances (induction cooktops, mixers) grew strongly, with kitchen appliances near 30% growth YoY, while coolers and fans declined on the delayed summer. Fans lost market share, mainly on BLDC gaps.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Consumer Products to bounce back in FY27, with the turnaround expected over the next quarter onward; no quantified guidance.
Intent to grow ahead of the market, which management sees at mid-single-digit; target to reach at least industry-average profitability of about 6-9% EBIT over time, with no firm timeline.
Lighting Solutions gross margin expected to stay positive, but part of the gain will be reinvested in growth so EBIT may stay near current levels.
Consumer Products FY25-level margins (about 3-3.5%) are difficult to commit to given war-related inflation; some cost may not be passed on.
Capex intensity to fall to less than half of past levels over the next two years, mainly for moulds and innovation.
Working capital to remain negative in FY27, as in the past two years.
capex_capacity: Capex for FY27 and FY28 expected to be less than half of past levels, mainly mould replacement and selected innovation spend.
Wires category launched in February 2026 in Lighting Solutions; growth targets to be tracked over the next 2-3 quarters.
Fans portfolio gap in BLDC to be bridged over the next 12 months; NEX BLDC product launched, scale-up plan under way.
demand_pricing: Consumer Products price increases of 3% to 10% taken in Q4 FY26, a similar range in April 2026, and further increases announced in May 2026 for war and commodity inflation.
Management says commodity inflation has been covered to the extent possible, but future price increases will be calibrated given demand uncertainty.
Channel inventory largely corrected; coolers still slightly elevated and fans need work. Summer demand is mixed: North recovering with a hot start, South strong, some areas hit by unseasonal rain.
Fan market share lost, mainly due to weak BLDC performance; industry's BLDC share is higher than Bajaj's.
Kitchen appliances, induction cooktops and mixers delivered double-digit growth; water heaters and irons grew modestly.
Management cites sentiment concerns from war, repeated price hikes and a patchy summer as key headwinds.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plan for FY27 and FY28, and segment-level revenue and margins for fans, appliances, wires and switchgear?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex will be less than half of past levels, mainly moulds and innovation. Kitchen appliances grew about 30%; coolers and fans declined on the delayed summer. Professional and Consumer Lighting both grew; wires is too new to split out margins.

qa_highlights.question: Can Lighting margins expand further in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Premium mix drove margin gains and should continue, but no target was given. Gross margin gains will be partly reinvested to accelerate growth, so EBIT may stay near current levels.

qa_highlights.question: When will Consumer Products momentum return, and can margins return to FY24/FY25 levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Excess trade stock has largely been flushed out; coolers still need some correction but are not material to the full year. Fans need work over the next 12 months. Returning to FY25 margins is difficult given war-related inflation; investment behind brands and innovation will step up over the next 12 months.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be more exceptional items?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said all identified issues have been addressed and expects a better next year, without quantifying any further exceptional items.

qa_highlights.question: Price increases taken and further increases needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Consumer Products price increases of 3%-10% in Q4 and a similar range in April, with more in May. Commodity inflation covered to the extent possible, with future increases to be calibrated.

qa_highlights.question: Channel inventory and summer demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Channel inventory corrected to a large extent; coolers still slightly elevated. Summer is mixed, with North recovering and South strong, plus some unseasonal rain.

qa_highlights.question: What do innovation and brand investments deliver, and what is the FY28-FY29 growth and margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to grow ahead of a mid-single-digit market and reach industry-average profitability of about 6-9% over time, with innovations priced to protect margin. No firm numbers were given.

qa_highlights.question: Fans market share trend and reason for the operating cash flow jump?
qa_highlights.answer: Fan market share has slipped, mainly on BLDC gaps. Operating cash flow was about INR 400 crore in Q4, half from inventory reduction and half from trade receivables.

qa_highlights.question: Will working capital stay at FY26 levels?
qa_highlights.answer: The company has run negative working capital for two years and expects to continue that in FY27.

risks_watch: Consumer Products stays loss-making or weak if the summer stays patchy and fans keep losing share on BLDC gaps.
Further price increases could hurt demand, while inflation may not be fully passed on, squeezing margins.
Lighting margin gains may be reinvested in growth, and the wires launch must hit its growth targets over the next 2-3 quarters.
Management did not rule out further exceptional items or write-offs; the CFO said issues found so far are addressed.
Coolers still have some channel inventory to correct, and the stated investment step-up in brands and innovation adds cost.
Leadership transition: new CFO Ashween Anand joined; Suketu Shah had been acting CFO.
summary.management_tone: Candid about a modest quarter and the Consumer Products weakness, but confident on Lighting and on a recovery in FY27. Management was evasive on specific margin and growth targets, repeatedly declining to give numbers beyond general intent.
key_quotes: We are confident of continuing this trajectory going forward.
Now most of that is out. The stock levels are now reasonable.
We know we are not competitive in fans. We recognize that.
So our intent going forward is to grow ahead of the market.

growth.why: No quantified revenue guidance; Consumer Products expected to bounce back in FY27 with no numbers, Lighting wires launched Feb 2026 with growth targets to be tracked over 2-3 quarters, and a 'grow ahead of market' intent (market mid-single digit) with no firm timeline, so growth outlook is flat-to-unclear.
